question: What is the fee for a Soroban transaction made of? Explain the inclusion fee, the resource fee, which part is refundable, and where rent fits.

golden.answer: The transaction fee is the resource fee plus the inclusion fee, which is the bid for a place in the ledger. The resource fee has a non-refundable part (CPU instructions, ledger read and write bytes, transaction size), charged on declared resources, and a refundable part (rent, events, return value), charged on actual use with the remainder refunded.
keyFacts: A Soroban transaction's fee is its resource fee plus its inclusion fee.
The non-refundable resource fee covers instructions, ledger I/O, and transaction size.
The refundable resource fee covers rent, events, and the return value.
Unused refundable fee is refunded after the transaction executes.
avoid: Do NOT say unused instructions or read and write bytes are refunded.
golden.notes: Do not require fee rates or stroop amounts; rates are set by validator vote. Accept 'bandwidth' or 'historical storage' for transaction size.

activation.author: gap lanes gap-1, gap-2, gap-3 (Claude Fable 5.2)

truth.notes: The fee split is protocol mechanism (CAP-0046-07, Final, Protocol 20) and has no volatile value; the scheduled tag follows the leaf, whose rates change by validator vote. CAP-0046-07 names the two parts competitiveResourcesFee and refundableResourcesFee, and refunds apply to failed transactions as well. One parallel-cli research run (core-fast, 2026-11-14) reproduced the split from the docs, the CAP and rs-soroban-env fees.rs with no disagreement. Boundary: q-soroban-simulate-resource-fee tests fee estimation by simulation; q-soroban-resource-limits tests limits.

sources.quote: Transaction Fee (Tx.fee) = Resource Fee (sorobanData.resourceFee) + Inclusion Fee
Non-refundable fees: calculated from CPU instructions, read bytes, write bytes, and bandwidth (transaction size, including its signatures).
Refundable fees: calculated from rent, events, and return value.
Protocol refunds that amount (when non-zero) to the transaction source account.
Fee computation library the docs call canonical (named by the docs page; not opened)
Total fee = inclusion fee + resource fee … Refundable: contract events size and invocation return value size, plus ledger space rent

corroboration.claim: A Soroban transaction's fee is the resource fee plus the inclusion fee.

evidence.note: The CAP defines the resource fee as a component of the transaction fee alongside the inclusion fee bid.

corroboration.claim: The non-refundable resource fee covers CPU instructions, ledger read and write bytes and transaction size; the refundable part covers rent, events and the return value.

evidence.note: effectiveRefundableFee is Events_fee plus Rent_fee; the competitive resources fee is charged on declared values.
Independent run reported the same split and no source disagreement.

corroboration.claim: Unused refundable fee is refunded to the source account after execution; unused declared instructions and I/O are not refunded.

evidence.note: Refund = sorobanData.resourceFee - resourceFee(tx) - effectiveRefundableFee, credited to the source account; 'No refund for unused capacity on market based resources'.
If the transaction uses fewer resources than declared, there will be no refunds (with a couple of exceptions); any unused refundable portion is refunded.

verified.by: verify-gap lane (Claude Opus 5.5) amendment of the gap proposal; applied by the instrument lane (Claude Opus 5.5), .agents/rounds/2026-11-14-golden-coverage-audit.md
evidence: The docs and CAP-46-07 confirm the split exactly: non-refundable for instructions, read and write bytes and bandwidth; refundable for rent, events and return value, charged on actual use. Freshness only: the golden pins no rate or date and the notes exclude fee rates, so 'scheduled' adds re-verification with no value. Make it stable.

Live A 2026-11-14: https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/fundamentals/fees-resource-limits-metering.md -- 'Non-refundable fees: calculated from CPU instructions, read bytes, write bytes, and bandwidth ... Refundable fees: calculated from rent, events'

Live B 2026-11-14: https://github.com/stellar/stellar-protocol/blob/master/core/cap-0046-07.md -- 'refundableResourcesFee - the maximum fee for resources that ... are charged based on the actual usage.'
